subject: API Model Cutover: compat gates, exception window & customer comms calendar
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed cutover & short exception window for AtlasPay (input needed)

Team —

Heads-up: AtlasPay (large payments customer, deal D-98421) asked for explicit timing on the upcoming model family cutover we announced for Nov. Their production traffic will be impacted by any change to the chat/model endpoint that changes tokenization/embedding outputs. They asked for a short exception window and for comms early so they can schedule their QA.

High-level ask: can we provide a 2-week backward-compatibility exception for AtlasPay during the cutover, and lock a comms calendar + a canned customer email by Oct 10? They are also asking for an explicit rollback plan.

Attached: cutover-proposal.xlsx (draft calendar, proposed canary cohorts). I want product + runtime to confirm feasibility for an exception lane (what bulk of requests we can accept without breaking SLOs) and engineering to confirm rollback steps. Sales needs a comms copy we can share with Samantha/Procurement.

Questions for the thread:
- Marissa: do product & policy allow a 2-week exception lane for one customer on this migration, and what guardrails would you want?
- Karthik: is a routing shim + compatibility gateway feasible as a stopgap? What are performance/cost tradeoffs?
- Ben/Naomi: what is the minimal comms plan Procurement needs to sign off?

Goal: align on a decision by Oct 10 so AtlasPay can freeze their test plan.

Thanks —
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Customer Success (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference

--

Date: 2028-10-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed cutover & short exception window for AtlasPay (input needed)

Sofia — thanks for the clear ask and the draft calendar. A few notes from Product/Platform POV: 

1) Exception lane: product is open to a narrow, timeboxed exception for one strategic customer, provided we have explicit SLA acknowledgements and an automated metric-based kill switch. We would require:
   - A scoped SLA exception (latency floors allowed but error-rate must stay <1.5%)
   - Canary cohort size and percent of traffic that will be routed to the old model vs new (recommend <=10% of critical endpoints)
   - Auto-fallback on error spikes (we can reuse the current fallback controller)

2) Compatibility gating: we can't guarantee identical embeddings/tokenization across model families. If their integration depends on exact vectors, we need a migration plan where AtlasPay runs both in parallel and validates similarity thresholds.

3) Rollback: engineering will need 24–48 hours to validate and execute a clean roll-back if necessary; in practice we will do progressive traffic shifts and monitor signals.

Action items:
- Karthik, can you confirm feasibility of a routing shim + cost estimate?
- Naomi / Ben, draft a comms template and an avoidance checklist for AtlasPay Procurement (we need to call out expected behavior, measurable validation steps, and a contact list).

I'll also schedule a short review with Platform to confirm the kill-switch metrics.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP Product
Redwood Inference

Sofia / Marissa —

Sales perspective: AtlasPay is highly sensitive to embedding drift; they currently run a heavy rerank + signature-match pipeline. Two immediate asks from Procurement and Samantha:

1) A formal comms calendar that shows blackout/QA windows, when we will flip traffic, and who to call during rollback. Procurement needs that in writing to sign the change.
2) A short test checklist (what endpoints to validate, sample payloads) they can plug into their CI so they can automate acceptance testing during the 2-week exception.

I drafted a customer-facing comm in comm-draft-atlaspay.md — see link. The key negotiation point: AtlasPay will accept a timeboxed exception if we commit to a maximum number of failed requests and to a response-time SLA for rollback coordination. Procurement asked us to include a DocuSign link (they want an addendum).

HubSpot ref: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/contact/67890 — I’ll attach the engagement notes.

Ben

Sofia / team —

Quick technical assessment from Runtime/Infra:

- Routing shim + compatibility gateway: feasible as an interim. Implementation notes:
  * We can route AtlasPay traffic to a pinned model binary (the older family) behind a tenancy flag. That will incur additional memory/GPU reservation and (~12–18% cost increase for the reserved window).
  * Latency impact minimal if we colocate the shim; KV cache warming is the main risk during the first 6 hours of the exception window.
  * We need a clean rollback API to switch routing at the edge within 15 minutes. Platform already has a partial flow; we’ll need 1 sprint to harden and test.

- Observability: suggest adding two extra metrics for the exception window: token-drift score (sampled), and rerank-similarity (daily). Those will feed the kill-switch thresholds.

Time/cost ask: one sprint of engineering (3 engineers) + minor infra ops changes. If Product/Pricing signs off, we can give AtlasPay a price for the exception lane (covering extra GPU footprint).

I’ll follow up with a short runbook draft by EOD Oct 5.

- Karthik

Subject: Re: Proposed cutover & short exception window for AtlasPay (decision + comms calendar)

Thanks everyone for the quick inputs — summary & next steps: 

Decision (agreed):
- We will offer AtlasPay a 10-business-day exception window starting Nov 6 (to align with their release cadence).
- The exception lane will route up to 12% of their critical traffic to the pinned model family.
- Kill-switch: auto-fallback on error-rate >1.5% OR token-drift score below agreed threshold.
- Cost: Sales will offer a temporary exception surcharge to cover reserved capacity; Ben to propose pricing addendum and a DocuSign link.

Owners & deliverables (due Oct 10):
- Karthik: runbook + rollback API spec + cost estimate (owner for infra tasks).
- Marissa: SLA exception doc and the explicit list of metrics for the kill-switch.
- Ben/Naomi: customer comms calendar and the procurement addendum (include sample CI checklist).
- Sofia: I’ll coordinate the customer pre-brief and schedule a 30-min sync with AtlasPay next week.

Samantha / Rajeev (AtlasPay) — if this looks reasonable, please confirm you can freeze your CI acceptance window and we’ll send the formal addendum & comms calendar by Oct 10.

Attachments: comm-draft-atlaspay.md (customer-facing email template).

Thanks —
Sofia
